Relaxed zoning regulations can lead to interesting juxtapositions, but equitable access to the city trumps subjective
because, even though it is smaller than the house, it was designed for more than one family. Photo by Dan Bertolet.
imgAlt: Small apartment building next to large house in Seattle. Photo by Dan Bertolet.
imgTitle: Relaxed zoning regulations can lead to unexpected juxtapositions, but equity trumps subjective aesthetics. Neither of these buildings would be legal in the 54 percent of Seattle’s land that is zoned single-family: the house, because it has been split up into perhaps a half dozen units; and the apartment, because, even though it is smaller than the house, it was designed for more than one family. by Dan Bertolet
